name: Hire to onboard: filling one professional job requisition
summary: This process fills one approved professional position, from the hiring manager's requisition through budget and HR approvals, advertising and sourcing, screening and interviews, the offer and its approvals, a background check and the new employee's first day. It involves the hiring manager, a department head, finance, an HR business partner, a recruiter and coordinator, an interview panel, HR operations, IT and outside parties (candidates, referees and a screening vendor). Most of the elapsed time is waiting: for approvers, for applications to arrive, for calendars to line up and for the candidate's notice period. It is error-prone where requirements are unclear at intake, where data is re-keyed from the applicant tracking system into the HR system, and where a slate produces no hire and sourcing starts again.

baseline.org_archetype: A US employer of about 2,000 people with a central talent acquisition team, an applicant tracking system separate from the HR information system, and an outside background screening vendor.
baseline.notes: Professional roles such as analysts, specialists and engineers at salaries of roughly 60,000 to 120,000 USD. Executive searches using agencies and high-volume hourly hiring follow different paths and are excluded.

trigger: A hiring manager needs to fill a vacancy left by a leaver or a new position in the approved plan and opens a requisition.
end_state: The new employee has completed the first day with paperwork, I-9, accounts and equipment in place; or the requisition is cancelled, the offer is withdrawn or the candidate reneges.

volume.seasonality: More requisitions open in January to March after budgets are set, fewer in December.

evidence.note: About 20% annual hiring for 2,000 staff gives 400 hires a year, of which about 40% are professional roles; 15 requisitions a month allows for cancellations. Author estimate.

triggered_by.from: Internal transfer or promotion that leaves a vacancy

produces.object: new employee record with pay and tax details

roles.title: Hiring manager
roles.department: Business function that owns the vacancy

systems.name: HR information system (employee and position records)
Applicant tracking system with requisition and offer approval workflow
Careers site, job boards and professional networking site
Headcount budget spreadsheet or planning model
Salary structure and market data spreadsheet

steps.name: Draft job requisition
steps.description: The hiring manager opens the requisition form in the applicant tracking system, picks or creates the position, writes the business justification, attaches or edits the job description and proposes a grade, salary range, location and target start date.

error.defect_description: Missing fields, outdated job description or a grade that does not match the work.

evidence.note: Fields and initiation by the manager are described by AIHR; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Department head approves headcount
steps.description: The department head receives the approval request by email, checks that the role is needed now and fits the department plan, and approves, returns it with questions or cancels it. Requests often wait while the approver travels or batches approvals weekly.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: budget holder approves new and replacement headcount

next.condition: returned for more justification or changes

evidence.note: Department head approval is a described step; probabilities and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Finance checks budget and cost centre
steps.description: The finance business partner compares the requested salary and cost centre with the approved headcount budget in the planning spreadsheet, confirms whether the post is a budgeted backfill or a new cost, and approves or rejects in the workflow.

error.defect_description: Wrong cost centre coded, found later in payroll costing.

control.basis: Headcount and budget control: finance sign-off for positions outside or above budget

next.condition: returned to re-scope level or salary
hiring freeze or budget not available

evidence.note: Finance budget approval is described by AIHR; shares are author estimates.

steps.name: HR validates grade and opens requisition
steps.description: The HR business partner checks the title and grade against the job architecture, sets the salary range from the salary structure, confirms the posting rules that apply (internal first, pay range disclosure for covered states) and releases the requisition with a number.

error.defect_description: Salary range set too low for the market, found when candidates decline or screen out on pay.

control.basis: Job architecture and pay equity policy: HR sets grade and range for every opened position

next.condition: returned for job description or grade rework

evidence.note: HR finalisation and requisition number described by AIHR; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Hold intake meeting with hiring manager
steps.description: The assigned recruiter books a 30 to 60 minute call with the hiring manager to agree must-have skills, the interview stages and panel, sourcing channels, target companies and the timeline, and records the plan in the applicant tracking system.

error.defect_description: Unclear or changing requirements, which later show up as a rejected shortlist.

evidence.note: Intake after approval is described by AIHR; the hiring manager's meeting time is not counted separately (author choice).

steps.name: Write and post job advert
steps.description: The recruiter turns the job description into an advert, adds the pay range and benefits summary where state law requires it, posts internally and on the careers site, and pushes the advert to paid and free job boards through the applicant tracking system.

error.defect_description: Missing pay range for a covered location, or advert text that does not match the role.

control.basis: Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (from January 2021) and similar local pay transparency laws: postings must state a good-faith pay range and describe benefits

evidence.note: Posting step from AIHR; the disclosure duty applies only to covered locations, so the control is conditional.

steps.name: Source candidates directly
steps.description: The recruiter searches the professional networking site, the applicant database and referrals for people who match the profile, sends personalised outreach messages and follow-ups, and adds interested people to the requisition.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Gem reports outreach sequences and reply rates for sourcing; hours are author estimates.

steps.name: Screen applications in the ATS
steps.description: After applications have built up for about a week, the recruiter reads each resume and screening answer in the applicant tracking system, rejects clear mismatches with a template email and moves a shortlist forward. A typical professional opening draws dozens to over a hundred applicants.

error.defect_description: A suitable applicant is rejected or left unreviewed.

next.condition: too few qualified applicants, more sourcing

evidence.note: 74 candidates per hire (Gem, 2021 to 2022) and about 121 applications per hire in early 2021 (Ashby); minutes per resume and the wait for applicants are author estimates.

steps.name: Hiring manager reviews shortlist
steps.description: The hiring manager opens the shortlisted profiles in the applicant tracking system, marks each as yes, maybe or no with a short comment, and sometimes asks the recruiter to recalibrate the search.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Recruiter phone screens
steps.description: The recruiter schedules and runs 20 to 30 minute phone screens with roughly five to eight candidates, checking motivation, salary expectations, notice period and work authorisation, and writes notes in the applicant tracking system.

error.defect_description: Salary expectation or notice period recorded wrongly, found at offer stage.

evidence.note: Glassdoor: a phone interview adds 6.8 to 8.2 days to the process; Gem: 11% of candidates reach the pre-onsite stage. Number of screens and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Hiring manager screening interviews
steps.description: The hiring manager holds 30 to 45 minute video interviews with the two to four strongest candidates, focusing on technical fit and team needs, and records a decision in the applicant tracking system.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: no one advances, back to sourcing

evidence.note: Glassdoor: each one-on-one interview stage adds 4.1 to 5.3 days. Pass rates and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Coordinate panel interview schedule
steps.description: The recruiting coordinator checks the calendars of four or five interviewers, proposes slots to each candidate, books video links or rooms, sends confirmations with the agenda, and reschedules when someone drops out.

error.defect_description: Double booking or wrong interviewer, causing a reschedule.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Conduct panel interviews and submit scorecards
steps.description: Four interviewers each spend 45 to 60 minutes with each of two or three finalists on a planned topic, then write a scorecard in the applicant tracking system and attend a short debrief. The wait covers finding dates that suit the candidates and a busy panel.

error.defect_description: Scorecards submitted late or without evidence, weakening the debrief.

evidence.note: Glassdoor: a panel stage adds 5.6 to 6.8 days; Ashby: about 12 interview hours per hire for business roles (recent data). Panel size and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Debrief and select finalist
steps.description: The hiring manager chairs the debrief, compares scorecards and decides whether to move a finalist to references, interview another candidate, reopen sourcing, or put the role on hold.

error.defect_description: A weak hire selected under time pressure.

next.condition: no hire from this slate, sourcing restarts
role put on hold or cancelled

evidence.note: Gem: 45% of onsite interviewees reach offer, so with two or three finalists roughly three quarters of slates yield a hire. The split of the remainder is an author estimate. Interview records from this step are retained for one year (EEOC).

steps.name: Check references
steps.description: The recruiter asks the finalist for two or three referees, emails them to book calls, asks a standard set of questions about past performance and records the answers. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for referees.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Company hiring policy: references before offer for professional roles

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022. Many employers skip or shorten references, which is why the control is discretionary.

steps.name: Prepare offer proposal
steps.description: The recruiter compares the candidate's expectations with the salary range, internal peers and market data, drafts base pay, bonus, start date and any sign-on payment, and enters the offer in the applicant tracking system for approval.

error.defect_description: Wrong figure or start date typed into the offer.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: HR checks offer against pay range and equity
steps.description: The HR business partner checks the proposed salary against the range and the pay of current staff in the same job, flags offers above the midpoint or with sign-on payments, and approves or sends back.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Compensation policy and pay equity review of every offer

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Department head approves offer
steps.description: The department head receives the offer approval request in the applicant tracking system or by email, checks the cost against budget and approves or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: a second manager above the recruiter and hiring manager approves compensation commitments

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Extend verbal offer
steps.description: The recruiter calls the candidate, presents the offer and benefits, answers questions and notes any counter request. A follow-up email summarises the terms.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Candidate considers offer
steps.description: The candidate weighs the offer, often against other offers or a counter-offer from the current employer, and then accepts, asks for better terms or declines.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: declines, return to runner-up or restart

evidence.note: Gem reports an 81% average offer acceptance rate (2021 to 2022); here 75% accept outright and some counters end in acceptance. The wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Issue written offer and collect signature
steps.description: The recruiter generates the offer letter from the template in the applicant tracking system, checks the merged fields, sends it for electronic signature with the contingencies stated, and chases the candidate until it is signed.

error.defect_description: Merged field wrong (salary, title or start date).

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Send disclosure and order background check
steps.description: The HR operations assistant sends the stand-alone background check disclosure and authorisation through the screening vendor portal, selects the package (criminal search, employment and education verification) and waits for the candidate to complete the form.

error.defect_description: Wrong package or misspelled name delays the check.

control.basis: Fair Credit Reporting Act: stand-alone written disclosure and written authorisation before obtaining a consumer report

evidence.note: Disclosure and permission duties are stated by the FTC; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Screening vendor completes checks
steps.description: The screening vendor searches county and federal court records, contacts past employers and schools, and posts the report. Delays come from courts without online access and former employers that do not answer.

error.defect_description: Record matched to the wrong person.

evidence.note: Vendor-stated traditional turnaround: county criminal 3 to 7 days, employment verification 5 to 10 days; Glassdoor: a background check adds 3.1 to 3.4 days to hiring.

steps.name: Review background report
steps.description: The HR operations assistant reads the report, compares employment dates and degrees with the resume, and either clears the candidate or flags a discrepancy or record for review under the company's screening policy.

error.defect_description: Discrepancy missed.

control.basis: Pre-employment screening policy: offers are contingent on a satisfactory check

evidence.note: Shares are author estimates; most flags are date or title discrepancies.

steps.name: Run pre-adverse action process
steps.description: HR sends the candidate a pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the report and the summary of rights, waits several business days for an explanation, reviews it with the HR business partner or counsel, and then clears the candidate or sends the final adverse action notice.
outputs: cleared candidate or adverse action notice

error.defect_description: Notice missing a required element, creating legal exposure.

control.basis: Fair Credit Reporting Act: pre-adverse action notice with report copy and summary of rights, then adverse action notice

evidence.note: Notice content stated by the FTC; the waiting period length and the outcome shares are author estimates (FTC does not fix a period).

steps.name: Create new hire record in the HRIS
steps.description: The HR operations assistant re-keys or imports the candidate's personal details, job, pay, manager and start date from the applicant tracking system into the HR information system, which triggers payroll, benefits and IT account requests.

error.defect_description: Typing error in salary, start date or bank details, usually found at the first payroll.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022. Many mid-sized firms still re-keyed between separate ATS and HRIS products.

steps.name: Provision accounts and equipment
steps.description: An IT support specialist picks up the new starter ticket, creates the directory and email accounts, assigns the software licences and access the manager requested, and images and ships or sets out a laptop before the start date.

error.defect_description: Missing access or late laptop, found on the first day.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022. Runs during the notice period.

steps.name: Wait for start date
steps.description: The new hire works out a notice period of about two weeks with the current employer while preboarding emails, benefits material and new hire forms are sent. A few candidates accept a counter-offer and withdraw in this period.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Preboarding after acceptance described by SHRM; the two-week notice norm and renege share are author estimates.

steps.name: First day paperwork and orientation
steps.description: On the first day HR examines the new hire's identity and work authorisation documents and completes Form I-9 Section 2, collects tax and direct deposit forms, explains benefits enrolment deadlines and runs the orientation session on policies and mandatory training.

error.defect_description: I-9 error or missing document, found in internal audit.

control.basis: Immigration Reform and Control Act: Form I-9 Section 2 within 3 business days of the first day of work for pay

evidence.note: Deadline stated by USCIS; orientation content described by SHRM; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Manager welcomes new hire and sets first-week plan
steps.description: The hiring manager meets the new hire, introduces the team and the onboarding buddy, checks that accounts and equipment work, walks through the first 30 days of goals and logs any missing access for IT.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Buddy and manager welcome described by SHRM; minutes are author estimates.

exceptions.name: No hire from the first slate
exceptions.description: The panel finds no suitable finalist or the shortlist is rejected, so the recruiter sources again and the interview cycle repeats, adding two to four weeks.

exceptions.name: Offer declined or countered
exceptions.description: The candidate declines (often for pay or a counter-offer) or asks for better terms; the offer is revised and re-approved, or the runner-up is approached.

exceptions.name: Requisition returned or cancelled during approval
exceptions.description: An approver returns the requisition for more justification, a grade change or a budget fix, or cancels it because of a hiring freeze.

exceptions.name: Background check discrepancy
exceptions.description: The report shows a criminal record or a mismatch in dates or degrees; HR follows the FCRA pre-adverse action process before clearing the candidate or withdrawing the offer.

exceptions.name: Candidate reneges before start
exceptions.description: The new hire accepts a counter-offer during the notice period; the requisition is reopened as a new case.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from requisition draft to the new hire's first day
benchmarks.population: Professional requisitions at mid-sized US employers (composite)

evidence.note: Composite: average time to fill of 43 days (requisition approval to offer acceptance, 2022) plus about one week for requisition approval (AIHR example) plus about three weeks from acceptance to start for background check and notice period (author estimate). The 43 days is a mean, so the median is likely somewhat lower; p90 is an author estimate.

benchmarks.unit: average calendar days from requisition approval to offer acceptance
benchmarks.population: Josh Bersin Company and AMS benchmark, 2022 (44 days in early 2023); professional services 47 days

benchmarks.unit: median days, candidate entry to hire
benchmarks.population: Gem customers, September 2021 to March 2022 (20 days non-technical, 39 technical)

benchmarks.unit: USD per hire, average (external costs and internal recruiting costs)

pain_points.description: Requisitions wait days for each approver in a serial chain (department head, finance, HR) before any recruiting starts.

evidence.note: AIHR describes the serial approval chain and an example of a week to approval.

pain_points.description: Scheduling interviews across several busy interviewers and candidates adds days per stage; each added interview stage lengthens the process.

evidence.note: Days added per screening method are stated by Glassdoor.

pain_points.description: Unclear requirements at intake lead to rejected shortlists and restarted sourcing.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

pain_points.description: Candidate data is re-keyed from the applicant tracking system into the HR system, causing pay and start date errors that surface at first payroll.

evidence.note: Author estimate from common practice at mid-sized US employers in 2019 to 2022.

pain_points.description: Background checks stall on court searches and unresponsive former employers, delaying start dates.

evidence.note: Causes of delay listed by a screening vendor.

pain_points.description: Candidates drop out or decline during long processes; offer acceptance averaged 81%.

assumptions: One requisition fills one position; a requisition with several openings is treated as several cases.

Touch time for each step is the summed hands-on time of the named role across all candidates handled at that step (for example all phone screens). The hiring manager's time in the intake meeting and the panel's debrief time are folded into s05 and s13.
The simulator adds step times in sequence; IT provisioning (s27) runs during the notice period and so has near-zero wait.
The cycle time benchmark is a composite of a published average time to fill and author estimates for approval and notice periods; no single source measures requisition draft to first day.
Pay transparency posting rules applied only in some states during 2021 and 2022 (for example Colorado); the control at s06 is mandatory only for covered locations.
Applicant records are kept for at least one year under EEOC rules; this retention is not modelled as a step.
Loaded hourly cost = BLS May 2021 median wage x 1.42 benefits factor (ECEC December 2021) x 1.15 overhead factor.
Recent figures from Ashby (2025 to 2026) are used only for interview-hours context; reference-period sources are preferred.
